record.body:
## Requirements

R1: `#/phase/<effort>/<phase>` renders the phase in the main pane, not in a dialog.
R2: For an effort with an area, the phase page breadcrumb reads `Product › <area title> › <effort> › <phase title>`.
R3: For an effort with no area, the phase page breadcrumb reads `Product › <effort> › <phase title>`.
R4: The phase page header shows the phase title.
R5: The phase page header shows the phase state.
R6: The phase page shows the chips of the phase.
R7: The phase page shows the next action of the phase.
R8: The phase page shows one button for each requirement of the phase.
R9: A requirement button on the phase page opens the requirement view as a modal.
R10: The phase page shows the tabs of the phase.
R11: `#/phase/<effort>/<phase>/tab/<tab>` opens the page on that tab.
R12: The phase page shows the task graph on the tab that carries it.
R13: The phase page shows the evidence board on the tab that carries it.
R14: The phase page shows the sections of the phase detail.
R15: The phase page has the same status tabs that the effort page has today.
R16: The phase page lists the tasks of the phase that match the selected status tab.
R17: A task row on the phase page opens the task view as a modal.
R18: The left rail on the phase page lists the phases of the effort.
R19: The left rail marks the current phase.
R20: The left rail folds the older done phases behind a button that shows them.
R21: The effort page lists the phases as rows, each with a progress bar.
R22: A phase row on the effort page links to `#/phase/<effort>/<phase>`.
R23: The effort page has no task table.
R24: The effort page has no status tabs.
R25: The existing leaf-view overlay tests pass unchanged.
R26: A leaf view opened from the phase page leaves the phase page in place behind it.
R27: Closing a leaf modal returns to the phase page URL.
R28: Esc on the phase page opens the effort page.
R29: The phase page writes nothing to the store.
R30: The Playwright test opens a phase page through the real server.

## Acceptance criteria

- R1 to R8, R10, R12 to R16, R18 to R24: unit tests in `dashboard/frontend/src` (vitest, jsdom) render the phase page and the effort page against fixture payloads.
- R9, R17, R25 to R27: unit tests click a requirement button and a task row and check the modal and the URL. The existing overlay tests for the other leaf views pass unchanged.
- R11: a router unit test parses `#/phase/<effort>/<phase>/tab/<tab>` and mounts the page on that tab.
- R28: a unit test dispatches Esc and checks the hash.
- R29: a unit test checks that the phase page issues no POST.
- R30: the Playwright test in `dashboard/frontend/e2e` passes locally and in CI.

## Constraints

- Phase `area-levels` is merged into `main` before this phase starts.
- Hash routing stays. The `#/phase/...` URL format does not change.
- The write buttons of the needs and backlog views stay in their modals, as today.
- No new dependencies.
- `npm run lint`, `npm run check`, `npm test` and `npm run build` pass. `src/api-types.ts` stays in sync.

## Non-goals

- Pages for the task, requirement, needs, backlog or record views.
- Changes to the `GET /api/phase` payload or to the tabs it returns.
- A redesign of the task graph or the evidence board.
- Any new write on the phase page.

## Invariants

- The URL decides the selected phase.
- The phase page is read-only.
- The page depth stops at the phase. Leaf views are modals.
- Every existing `#/phase/...` deep link still opens that phase.

## Assumptions

- Phase `area-levels` provides the breadcrumb and the level-aware left rail.
- The existing view models for chips, next action, requirements, task graph, task list, evidence and sections can feed a page.
- `GET /api/phase` carries what the modal shows today.
